contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned what an akhaan is. Today: your first real Punjabi proverb!

ਦੂਰ ਦੇ ਢੋਲ ਸੁਹਾਵਣੇ literally means 'drums sound sweeter from far away' — it's used when something looks better or more appealing from a distance than it actually turns out to be up close, similar to the English saying 'the grass is greener on the other side.' Write a short example of a time (real or made up) when something seemed exciting from far away but turned out to be less exciting up close, and explain how it connects to this proverb.
You just learned your first real Punjabi proverb! Tomorrow we'll learn a second one about what's close to home.

objectives: Understand the meaning of ਦੂਰ ਦੇ ਢੋਲ ਸੁਹਾਵਣੇ
Write a personal example connecting to the proverb's lesson
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's akhaan-definition work briefly.
2. Introduce ਦੂਰ ਦੇ ਢੋਲ ਸੁਹਾਵਣੇ and its literal + figurative meaning.
3. Have the child write a connecting personal example.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's second proverb.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a concrete example first (a movie that looked exciting in the trailer but was disappointing) as a model to adapt
Ready for more: ask the child to compare this proverb directly to the English 'the grass is greener' saying — what's the same, what's different
Real, well-known Punjabi proverbs (not invented ones) — accuracy matters here the same way it does for any other Gurmukhi content on this platform
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended activity — check that the child's example genuinely reflects the proverb's lesson: something appealing from a distance that was less impressive up close.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's literature-excerpts thread with a real, well-known Punjabi proverb, continuing this week's introduction to the akhaan genre.
